body: Investors earn less than the funds they own because they buy after gains and sell after falls. Morningstar measured a gap of about **1.2 points a year** in the US over the ten years to 2025, widening to 2.1 points in the most volatile funds ([Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/business/insights/research/mind-the-gap-2025)). In India, Axis MF found equity and hybrid funds returned about **19.1% a year from 2003 to 2022 while the average investor earned about 13.8%** ([Axis MF](https://www.axismf.com/cms/sites/default/files/pdf-factsheets/Thinking%20Aloud%20-%20Using%20your%20Mutual%20Funds%20More%20Effectively.pdf)). Over 30 years, that gap compounds to roughly a 4x difference in ending wealth. Even Lynch's investors lagged him: one estimate puts their dollar-weighted return at 13.4% against the fund's 21.8% over 1981–1990 ([CBS MoneyWatch](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/lessons-from-a-great-fund-managers-record)). Barber and Odean found the most active fifth of traders netted 11.4% a year against 18.5% for the least active, with gross returns similar, so costs ate the difference ([Odean](https://faculty.haas.berkeley.edu/odean/Papers%20current%20versions/Individual_Investor_Performance_Final.pdf)). Investors also sell winners too early and hold losers too long, and the winners they sell go on to beat the losers they keep ([Odean, 1998](https://faculty.haas.berkeley.edu/odean/papers/disposition/disposition.html)).

**Mohnish Pabrai (*The Dhandho Investor*, 2007)**
- **The nine principles.** They include investing in existing businesses, simple businesses, distressed businesses in distressed industries, businesses with durable moats, few bets/big bets/infrequent bets, arbitrage, margin of safety, and "low risk, high uncertainty." — [Manas Saloi book summary](https://manassaloi.com/booksummaries/2016/03/14/mohnish-pabrai-the-dhandho-investor.html); [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/338613/the-dhandho-framework)
- **Asymmetry (said).** "Heads I win; tails I don't lose much." — [Outlook Money](https://www.outlookmoney.com/invest/mohnish-pabrais-lessons-in-the-dhandho-of-investing)
- **Cloning (said).** Pabrai calls himself a "shameless cloner" of Buffett, Munger and others. — [Antoine Buteau, lessons from Pabrai](https://www.antoinebuteau.com/lessons-from-mohnish-pabrai/)
- **Evolution (commentary).** Later commentary says his approach has shifted toward growth with a value bent. — [Outlook Money](https://www.outlookmoney.com/invest/mohnish-pabrais-lessons-in-the-dhandho-of-investing)

**Terry Smith (Fundsmith)**
- **Mantra (said).** "Buy good companies, don't overpay, do nothing." Fundsmith: "We only buy shares in good companies, try not to overpay and then do nothing." — [Fundsmith](https://www.fundsmith.co.uk/news/2015/2171-this-is-money-firms-which-provide-good-products-or-services-are-key-to-investing-says-fundsmith-boss/); [Smithson/Fidelity "three steps"](https://smithson.co.uk/news/2015/2036-fidelity-three-steps-to-heaven)
- **Primary test.** The key test is a high ROCE across the economic cycle. Holdings typically earn 25–30% ROCE. — [Trustnet](https://www.trustnet.com/news/662915/three-simple-steps-to-making-returns-like-terry-smith)
- **Conflicting thresholds.** Blogs cite 15–20% or "20%+" ROCE, and one lists interest coverage >15x. These are lower-quality secondary sources. — [MarketScreener](https://in.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Legendary-investor-Terry-Smith-44733685)
- Fundsmith's annual owner letters also stress high gross margins, high cash conversion and a FCF yield-based valuation [primary, not re-fetched].

body:
`strategy:smith-quality-do-nothing` | confidence: **verified** | tags: global, process, quality, low-turnover

Rule 1 - good companies: high ROCE in cash terms, high gross margins (pricing power), high cash conversion, low leverage, growth that can be reinvested, resilience to obsolescence; avoid banks, heavy cyclicals, airlines, conglomerates. Rule 2 - don't overpay: compare free-cash-flow yield with bond yields and the company's growth. Rule 3 - do nothing: minimise turnover and trading costs; let compounding work. Measured over 2010-2025 the approach beat MSCI World (13.8% vs 12.1% a year) but lagged five calendar years in a row (2021-25), when mega-cap tech concentration, passive flows and de-rating of 'quality defensives' hurt. Indian application: the checklist is close to the Marcellus/consistent-compounder template; the binding constraint in India is rule 2 - quality FMCG/consumer names at 60-80x earnings can deliver low single-digit returns for years even as earnings grow.
